summary.text: An 81-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, coronary heart disease and hypertension was admitted in August 2019 after a lung nodule was found incidentally on physical examination, without clinical symptoms. He underwent thoracoscopic wedge resection with mediastinal lymph node dissection. Pathology confirmed adenocarcinoma with tumor thrombus in interstitial vessels and visceral pleura invasion, staged pT2aN0M0, stage IB, and he refused adjuvant therapy.

After 14 months without progression, chest CT and PET-CT on October 27, 2020 showed mediastinal and supraclavicular lymph node metastasis. Sequencing of archived tumor tissue detected a KIF5B-RET fusion without co-alterations in EGFR, ALK, ROS1, MET, HER2, BRAF or KRAS. The ECOG score was 2 and he refused chemotherapy. First-line alectinib began on November 15, 2020, with stable disease and hypertension, until progression in July 2021.

Second-line pralsetinib 400 mg once daily started on July 10th, 2021. After grade 2 hypertension, grade 1 platelet and neutrophil suppression and grade 1 AST elevation, the dose was reduced to 300 mg and then 200 mg per day, with monthly CT showing stable disease. On November 29th, 2021 CT showed new nodules and biopsy showed PAS-positive cryptococcus spores, diagnosing pulmonary cryptococcosis without signs of meningitis; fluconazole was followed by voriconazole after lesion growth.

On March 3, 2022 he was hospitalized with fever, purulent cough and hemoptysis; sputum culture grew MSSA, a lung abscess was treated with intravenous biapenem and he improved. On April 7, 2022 dyspnea and pericardial and bilateral pleural effusions with adenocarcinoma cells indicated progression with liver metastasis. Intrapleural and pericardial chemotherapy controlled only the pericardial effusion; he became bedridden with ECOG 4, developed respiratory distress and died on June 21, 2022.

ambiguities.issue: The case text places the incidentally found nodule in the right upper lobe on admission, but the wedge resection two weeks later is described as of the left upper lobe. The source does not reconcile the lobe laterality.

evidence.quote: with an incidental finding of a nodule in the right upper lobe during a physical examination
the patient underwent thoracoscopic wedge resection of the left upper lobe

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not decide which side is correct or assign laterality to the nodule, resection or primary tumor; the nodule and the resection themselves are not in dispute.

ambiguities.issue: The discussion states that pralsetinib may not be the only factor in the lung infections and attributes the cryptococcal route and Staphylococcus aureus source only as possibilities; the case text does not state a cause for either infection.

evidence.quote: Indeed, pralsetinib may not be the only factor contributing to the infectious events in this case.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record pralsetinib, pigeon dust or nasal colonization as an established cause of the infections.
